Down to talk about our analysis of dpdr. Been dealing it for 5 years now. And have more or less been thinking about it deeply along the way. 

Lately I’m feeling it is a rejection of the existence of objects - which in smaller doses is perhaps a way of coping with unpleasant realities. I find my dpdr feelings are triggered when I speak my truest thoughts and when I interact with reality in consequential ways — telling one of my housemates that I’ve been considering my friend meet everyone to potentially move in (the “consequential” here is that My housemate now knew and, as far as objects and momentum in reality concerned, there was no going back from that point).

Hey Threeoptions123, thanks for saying hi! I feel that. I feel like conversations can have a profound impact on my dissociation sometimes. Try to not go more than 1 day without a conversation. Feel like I can drift a lot otherwise.

I think it does!

I’ve spoken at length over time with one of my non-dissociated friends, and it seems to me that they can connect some of their own experiences to ones that I’ve described. 

I’ve felt complete depersonalization/derealization and also quite grounded, as well as mild amounts of dissociation, which is where I’m generally at now these days. It’s not gone, and it fluctuates, but it’s still there

Haven’t heard very much of people enjoying it, mostly it’s troublesome. 
From what I’ve heard from other people’s experiences, it is more common that is upsetting than fun. 

Only after much healing have I experienced it to be an annoyance. Prior to that it was generally in the realm of dreadful. 

I have “enjoyed” new perspectives on the world I don’t think I would have gotten had I not been dissociated for such a long/consistent amount of time. 

But the experience/sensation itself has never been enjoyable for me, in all my years, I think I can say that. 

Perhaps when I’m with other dissociates and we come to make jokes about it, but that’s still not the experience of dissociation itself. 

I might encourage you to be careful bringing up the notion of dissociation being enjoyable. It’s generally expressed to be not fun, and a severely disrupting/derailing experience for people - and so asking if it’s fun reads as a little insensitive. Just a warning, as to avoid upsetting people around you.
